source_text: This perspective aligns with bioethical reviews arguing that true proxy consent requires demonstrable net benefit without alternatives, a threshold unmet by circumcision's modest, proxy-derived advantages versus certain sensory losses and psychological impacts reported in adult surveys. [142]
